title: Two-step nilpotent minimal-graph-admissibility conjecture
statement: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-step nilpotent Lie algebra. **Nilpotent minimal-graph-admissibility conjecture.** If $k\leq 2$, then $\mathfrak{g}$ is minimal-graph-admissible; if $k>2$, then $\mathfrak{g}$ is not necessarily minimal-graph-admissible, and there exist $k$-step nilpotent Lie algebras that fail to be minimal-graph-admissible. The motivation is that adjoint actions commute in the two-step case, whereas this need not hold for three-step nilpotent Lie algebras; the conjecture remains open.
references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2017–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2505.07632](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.07632), [arXiv:2007.02140](https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.02140), [arXiv:1710.03972](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.03972).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.16161

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2026). “We now present a selection of open problems and conjectures that naturally arise from our findings.”
source_name: Tim Heib and David Edward Bruschi, “On the structural properties of Lie algebras via associated labeled directed graphs”, arXiv:2601.16161 (2026).
